answer: No. Your records show you did not have a blood clot in your lung. In July 2025 you had chest wall pain, and a blood test (D-dimer) came back mildly raised at 0.92 (normal is up to 0.49). That test can be high for many reasons, so you had a CT scan of the chest with contrast that same day to look for a clot. The report says there was no pulmonary embolism and your lungs were clear. Pulmonary embolism is recorded as 'ruled out', and the chest wall pain was marked resolved by 22 July 2025. The scan only showed mild wear-and-tear changes in the spine of your upper back.
short: A CT angiogram of the chest on 8 July 2025, done after a raised D-dimer, showed no pulmonary embolism; the diagnosis is recorded as ruled out.

knowledge.says: D-dimer is sensitive but not specific for clots; a positive result is followed by imaging such as CT pulmonary angiography, and a negative CT effectively excludes a clinically important embolism.
